Bruno Maçães's book The Dawn of Eurasia: On the Trail of the New World Order is part of a growing body of literature on the subject of developing connectivity and integration between Europe and Asia. The concept of Eurasia is defined in various ways, though often referring to post-Soviet countries. Maçães goes beyond this and explores—both literally and figuratively—a Eurasian supercontinent, spanning the two continents in their entirety, and representing global economic and political power players. He argues that in order for Europe, in particular the European Union, to avoid being left behind, greater attention must be paid to investing in stronger relationships with Asian countries.
